lines.text: Mind the shears. The cart's narrower than it looks.
Jasper Crane said I might find you.
Did he. He owes me for a coat.

Here's how it goes. You bring me something plain, and something small that's been somewhere. A shard. A bit of wall. A button off somebody's shirt. I sew the one into the other, and after that it does a small thing, every time.
One charm to a piece, and that's all a cart can do. Finer needlework wants a proper shop, and a bigger town than this.
Back again. Let's see what you've got.
Not the button. The thread. Nobody else waxes it like that.
It was in a goose's heap on the road.
Then he hasn't got the coat on, has he. It's walking about on somebody else.
I'll put it on his slate. That makes four.
